clean_methods: Context: To address the central question of whether DA and 5-HT systems interact in the striatum, the proposal uses the method: We will employ a multi-methodological approach combining optogenetics, fiber photometry with genetically-encoded neurotransmitter sensors, and slice electrophysiology to investigate the bidirectional interactions between DA and 5-HT systems.

Context: To test causal effects of dopamine neuron activity on striatal neurotransmitter release, the proposal uses the method: We will test whether optogenetic stimulation of VTA DA neurons results in DA and/or 5-HT release in the striatum.

Context: To test causal effects of serotonergic neuron activity on striatal neurotransmitter release, the proposal uses the method: We will test whether stimulation of DRN SERT neurons produces release of DA or 5-HT in the striatum.

Context: To identify synaptic mechanisms underlying observed crosstalk, the proposal uses the method: For electrophysiological investigations, we will use whole-cell patch-clamp recordings in acute brain slices to examine synaptic connections and potential glutamate co-release from serotonergic neurons, as DR projections have been reported to release glutamate in addition to serotonin.

Context: To map regional synaptic inputs from DRN SERT neurons, the proposal uses the method: We will combine optogenetic projection targeting with whole-cell recordings to parse synaptic currents in identified regions including the DS, anterior and posterior NAc shell, orbitofrontal cortex (OFC), and VTA.

Context: To isolate excitatory synaptic contributions from serotonergic projections, the proposal uses the method: We will use NBQX/AP5 to block glutamatergic transmission and determine whether DRN SERT neurons make excitatory synapses onto neurons in these regions.
Context: To enable cell-type-specific manipulation and measurement, the proposal uses the method: We will use DAT-IRES-Cre and SERT-Cre transgenic mice to achieve cell-type specific targeting.

Context: To express an optogenetic actuator in the targeted midbrain populations, the proposal uses the method: For optogenetic stimulation, we will inject AAV8-syn-Flex-Chrimson-tdTomato into either the VTA of DAT-Cre mice or the DRN of SERT-Cre mice.

Context: To measure striatal neurotransmitter release in real time, the proposal uses the method: To monitor neurotransmitter release, we will inject AAV5-CAG-dLight1.2 for DA detection or AAV9-hSyn-5-HT3.0 for 5-HT detection into the nucleus accumbens (NAc) and dorsal striatum (DS).

Context: To standardize optogenetic activation across experiments, the proposal uses the method: We will deliver optogenetic stimulation consisting of 5 pulses, each composed of 30 bursts separated by 250 ms (each burst consisting of 5 laser pulses of 4-ms pulse width at 20 Hz).

Context: To validate in vivo sensor responses and provide a positive control, the proposal uses the method: We will use fiber photometry to record neurotransmitter dynamics in real-time and compare responses to passive cocaine injection (15mg/kg) as a positive control.

Context: To prepare mice for in vivo recording, the proposal uses the method: After 4-5 weeks of viral expression, we will habituate mice to handling and connection cables for three days before testing.

Context: To standardize the in vivo recording session, the proposal uses the method: On testing days, we will place mice in a transparent open-field chamber for 3 minutes of habituation, followed by 5 minutes of baseline recording, optogenetic stimulation, another 5 minutes of baseline recording, cocaine injection (15mg/kg i.p.), and 40 minutes of additional recording.

Context: To quantify in vivo neurotransmitter responses, the proposal uses the method: We will analyze fiber photometry data using MATLAB, computing ΔF/F signals and normalizing to baseline. We will measure area under the curve for 5-second windows during baseline and after stimulation, and compare peak signals after optogenetic stimulation to those after cocaine injection.

Context: To quantify excitatory synaptic responses in acute slices, the proposal uses the method: For electrophysiology, we will record optogenetic EPSCs with single or paired pulses at 0.1 Hz in the presence of picrotoxin to isolate excitatory currents.
